title: 2027 Tax Brackets
summary: Explore the IRS inflation-adjusted 2027 tax brackets, for which taxpayers will file tax returns in early 2028.

title: EU Tax Omnibus Proposal: Suggestions for Improving Its Legal Design and Increasing Its Political Viability
summary: Tax Foundation Europe's input to the European Commission’s public consultations on the Tax Omnibus proposal reviews selected issues that have an impact on growth and competitiveness.

title: The State Tax Competitiveness Index Is Your Guide to Economic “Wins Above Replacement”
summary: Taxes are an important part of the mix, and modernizing a state’s tax structure helps position it for growth. States that rank better on the Index have better-structured tax codes, and states with better-structured tax codes get Wins Above Replacement.

title: 2027 State Tax Competitiveness Index
summary: The State Tax Competitiveness Index enables policymakers, taxpayers, and business leaders to gauge how their states’ tax systems compare. While there are many ways to show how much state governments collect in taxes, the Index evaluates how well states structure their tax systems and provides a road map for improvement.

title: What a Democratic Congress Means for Federal Tax Policy in 2027
summary: With Democrats retaking control of the US House of Representatives and US Senate, several new federal tax issues are on the table for 2027.

title: How Tax Policy Fared on the Ballot in 2026
summary: In red and blue states alike, voters showed wariness toward novel changes to the tax code, with two notable exceptions.

title: UK Autumn Budget Prioritizes Short-Term Relief over Long-Term Growth
summary: The UK’s 2026 Autumn Budget largely favors short-term relief over growth, highlighting the need for pro-growth reforms such as replacing the Stamp Duty Land Tax with annual property or land taxes.

title: Economic Education Includes Addressing Tax Confusion
summary: Economics isn’t just a course with supply and demand graphs and a quirky usage of “guns and butter.” It’s a discipline focused on incentives and responses, and we can see its impact all around us, shaping our world and our choices.

title: What Is the US Debt Limit and Why Does It Matter?
summary: The debt limit is one of Congress’s few chances to debate unsustainable borrowing, and reforms should create more room for bipartisan deficit reduction, not less.

title: Congress Has a Chance to Improve the Taxpayer Experience in 2026
summary: The Senate recently passed the Taxpayer Assistance and Service Act, which contains 65 provisions to improve tax administration and the IRS.

title: Pillar Two Implementation in Europe, 2026
summary: 22 of the 27 EU Member States have implemented both the income inclusion rule and the qualified domestic minimum top-up tax in 2026.

title: New Research Finds That Revenue-Maximizing Top Tax Rate Likely Lower Than Previous Estimates
summary: A new paper shows raising top income tax rates on the current tax base may not yield as much revenue as previously estimated, due to opportunities to shift income to different tax bases within the tax code.

title: Property Tax Relief on the Ballot: Three Approaches, One Clear Winner
summary: This November, states across the country are asking voters to consider changes to their state constitutions to address the burden of rising property taxes.

title: A “Token Tax” Could Kill the Promise of AI
summary: If we want to ensure that AI raises economic growth, we shouldn’t be pursuing tax policies that are stuck in the past and represent some of the worst ideas from the early internet age.

title: How Much Does the US Government Lose to Tax Fraud?
summary: While the government will never close the tax gap or fully eliminate tax fraud, lawmakers and the IRS can institute several reforms to reduce the gap, including simplifying the tax code, increasing third-party information reporting, and coordinating anti-fraud efforts.

title: 2027 Tax Foundation Europe Gala
summary: Join us on Monday 27 September 2027 for Tax Foundation Europe’s second annual Gala. Hear from leading experts, network over dinner, and celebrate the pan-European tax policy community.

title: 2027 Tax Foundation Europe Conference
summary: Join us for Tax Foundation Europe’s 2027 Conference, where we will bring together leaders from the international tax community to discuss major tax topics, hear from top academics on new research, and more.

title: Could an Employer Compensation Tax Save Social Security?
summary: With Social Security insolvency rapidly approaching and policymakers exploring changes to benefits and taxation, Congress could look to base-broadening reforms like the ECT as a guide for how to think about taxing compensation and broadening the tax base.

title: Cigarette Taxes and Cigarette Smuggling by State, 2024
summary: Cigarette smuggling is costly for states. We estimate that the forgone revenue from smuggled cigarettes totaled more than $4.6 billion in 2024. California lost nearly $1.4 billion in cigarette excise tax collections, and New York missed out on more than $1.2 billion.

title: Spain’s Tax Competitiveness Has Declined Since 2018
summary: Under Spain’s current Social Democratic government, the country has fallen from 27th to 35th (out of 38 OECD countries) in the International Tax Competitiveness Index.
